the new approach to problems of multiplicity is a practical and powerful alternative to the traditional approach.

, in problems with multiple significance tests, the control of the expected proportion of type I errors among the rejections the false discovery rate is often a more appropriate goal than is that of controlling the familywise type I error probability, and the new procedure is a simple and practical way of doing so.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the control of the FWER should not be viewed as the only legitimate goal in multiple testing.
the false discovery rate is often a better error rate to control than the FWER and that controlling the former is easier and more powerful than the latter.
controlling the false discovery rate is a more flexible approach to multiple testing than controlling the familywise Type I error.
